rules.rationale: Free-will belief and determinism belief are not logical opposites; compatibilist combinations are possible.
Agency-family classification must be derived and explicitly confirmed rather than inferred from one slider.
Atheism/theism and naturalism/supernaturalism are related but not conceptually identical.
Deity belief does not determine physicalism or nonphysicalism.
Physicalism and nominalism concern different ontological questions.
Moral stance-independence does not by itself entail universal applicability.
Moral realism/objectivity does not entail generalism over particularism.
Metaethical family must synthesize multiple logically distinct commitments.
Sensitivity to consequences does not entail permissiveness toward instrumental harm.
Consequential considerations and deontic constraints can both be strongly endorsed.
Individualism and collectivism are independently measurable orientations, not forced complements.
Authority as a moral foundation is not the same construct as legitimacy of coercive political authority.
Equality as a moral foundation is not identical to any specific distributive-justice principle.
Revelation can be measured as an epistemic source and as a religious authority; the scores must remain distinct.
Belief in deity existence does not determine how central religion or spirituality is in a person's life.
Private theological belief does not determine support for religious authority in public law.
Political legitimacy and a general obligation to obey are distinct philosophical claims.
Noninterference liberty and positive/capability liberty may both be valued strongly.
Market and democratic/collective coordination preferences need not sum to a fixed total.
Retribution, deterrence, and rehabilitation/restoration are independent purposes of punishment.
Transformation scenarios interpret personal-identity commitments; they do not replace the underlying construct.
Existential response is a secondary interpretation of meaning-related commitments.
Biological, environmental, conscious-reason, and unconscious explanations can all contribute simultaneously.
Group dominance and anti-egalitarianism are related but separately measurable.
Breadth of moral concern and impartial beneficence overlap but are not identical.
Belief that objective meaning is absent does not logically entail pessimism or resignation.
Naturalism does not entail reductionism.
Detailed deity-model questions are only meaningful when some deity-like reality is entertained.
Intervention questions presuppose at least some supernatural commitment or live possibility.
Detailed divinity classification follows a deity/divinity branch.
Detailed consciousness-theory branching should use the respondent's reducibility stance as routing information, not as a forced classification.
Metaethical anti-realism must never be inferred from social tolerance or vice versa.
Epistemic fallibilism/open revision must never be defined by support for a particular political institution.
Social-construction beliefs must not be inferred from left/right distributive preferences.
Supernatural belief and moral purity concern different constructs and must not proxy for each other.
Fallible propositional judgments and contextual certainty need not exclude one another.
Foundational warrant does not entail infallibility.
Revisable human concepts do not entail a mind-dependent physical world.
A priori rationalism is not the same as reasoning from sensory evidence.
Abstract objects and universals require separate evidence.
Easy ontology is not automatically abstract-object nominalism.
A deflationary method is not automatically external-world anti-realism.
Institution-dependent reality does not imply normative collectivism.
Individual-level explanation is not a moral priority rule.
Psychological and ethical egoism must not proxy for one another.
Practical rationality and moral rightness are distinct normative questions.
Ownness is not an obligation to maximize self-interest.
Ownness need not exclude elective concern for others.
Rejecting categorical reasons does not by itself reject objective life-conditional ethics.
Promissory reasons and exit conditions are not an all-or-nothing opposition.
Withdrawal can coexist with reliance-based repair responsibilities.
Promise morality and contractual enforceability require separate questions.
Strong property protection does not uniquely identify a natural-rights foundation.
Status and instrumental justifications can coexist.
No general obedience duty does not entail useless government.
Philosophical anarchism does not by itself prescribe state abolition.
Polycentric governance is not synonymous with nonstate market law.
Permission to coerce in a case does not entail exclusive territorial authority.
Ordinary agency and a condition excluding determinism are different claims.
